races.name: Winning Experience With Moulton Racing Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: Dream Illusion
runners_data.note: Has placed twice over 7f on good ground and is Michael Herrington's best-credentialed runner at this level; sits naturally just off the pace and is well-positioned to press Lovers Leap throughout from stall draw — 34 days since last run is within normal range.
runners_data.comment: Two runner-up efforts sandwich a blank run in her recent form, and a success sits further back too, with today's trip and ground form already banked. Fourth of eight on our figures; the 34-day gap since her last start is the main query.

runners_data.name: Ironist
runners_data.note: George Margarson's filly brings two placed efforts at 7f on good ground and was back just 9 days ago suggesting she is in a good rhythm; Mason Paetel's 5lb claim softens the weight burden materially and she should track the leader comfortably from a prominent pitch.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in her last five starts, Ironist has been competitive throughout — two 4ths and a 3rd before fading to 5th then 8th last time. A quick 9-day turnaround and proven form at today's trip and on this ground keep her live for a leading role.

runners_data.name: Izzy Fast
runners_data.note: Hector Crouch takes the mount on this filly who won last time at 6f on good going and now steps up to 7f — the extra distance may help her hold-up style; 41 days off is manageable, and on a flat track with a clean run she is the most likely beneficiary if the race develops into a proper test.
runners_data.comment: Hard to fancy on this evidence: Izzy Fast's last two starts brought a 7th and a 9th, some way below the level of the win she landed three runs back. A 41-day absence adds to the concerns, though she has today's trip and ground covered.

runners_data.name: Fantasy Obsessor
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's filly carries a hood and has a strong record of placing over shorter trips on good and standard going; her natural running style is hold-up, though with several genuine rear-dwellers in this field she is likely to find herself further forward than ideal, which tempers her chance.
runners_data.comment: A picture of consistency without troubling the judge, Fantasy Obsessor has three runner-up efforts among her last six starts and already has today's trip and ground covered. First-time cheekpieces add intrigue, though the yard is out of form — just one success from its last 21 runners.

runners_data.name: Lovers Leap
runners_data.note: Jane Chapple-Hyam's 3yo is the only genuine front-runner in the field and has course form, having won over a mile at Yarmouth on good going — stepping back to 7f suits her speed profile; Billy Loughnane can set the fractions to suit and the lack of a pace rival is a significant tactical advantage.
runners_data.comment: Lovers Leap sets the standard on our figures, landing a race two starts back and rarely finishing far away in this sequence. She's proven over today's trip and ground; a below-par run last time and the 46-day gap are the only reservations.

runners_data.name: Angels' Share
runners_data.note: William Knight sends out this filly who won over 7f on standard going but has been well beaten in four subsequent starts on good and soft turf; Cieren Fallon takes over and she will need things to fall perfectly from off the pace on ground that may be quicker than ideal for her.
runners_data.comment: A win sits at the back of Angels' Share's recent form, but four finishes outside the frame since — an unplaced effort, two 8ths and a 9th — are hard to ignore. Today's trip and ground are covered, and a 25-day break gives her a chance to bounce back.

runners_data.name: Allegrino
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's 3yo arrives with a fine recent record including a win and two places over 6-7f on standard and good going; William Buick is a strong booking and his natural running style is prominent, though with pace already established ahead of him he is likely to find himself in midfield rather than his preferred spot — discount slightly.
runners_data.comment: Consistency is Allegrino's calling card — no finish worse than 3rd across her last five starts, including a win three runs back. Even so, she's rated bottom of this field on our figures and it's unclear whether today's ground will suit, since only the trip is proven.

runners_data.name: Galileo Charm
runners_data.note: Marco Botti's 3yo won over this exact trip on standard going and has placed twice at 7f on similar; 50 days off is the longest break in the field and Robert Havlin rides — a genuine prominent type who is likely to be shuffled back given the pace ahead of him, which works against a horse who races best when holding a forward position.
runners_data.comment: Galileo Charm's form has tailed off with back-to-back 7ths, though further back she landed a race and was frequently competitive, including a 2nd and 3rd. First-time cheekpieces and a 50-day break could freshen her up, but the recent dip leaves her only sixth of eight on our figures.

races.paceDynamic: Lovers Leap is the lone confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner flat 7f contest at Yarmouth on good-to-firm ground, and with no genuine challenger likely to press her from the off, she can control the tempo from the gates and set a measured, sustainable pace throughout. Dream Illusion and Ironist are the natural prominent horses best placed to track her in the first two or three lengths, giving this race a fairly orderly early shape with a clear leader and a small group in attendance. The hold-up contingent — Izzy Fast, Angels' Share, Fantasy Obsessor — will be settled in the rear, waiting for the tempo to sharpen in the final two furlongs on this flat track where late closers can often find a clear run. This shape favours horses who can travel prominently just off the steady early pace and produce a controlled finish, specifically those sitting second or third in the group behind Lovers Leap; note that the field holds more prominent and hold-up types than the map can accommodate — Allegrino, Galileo Charm, and Fantasy Obsessor are genuine prominent or hold-up horses who are unlikely to secure their natural position, with Dream Illusion and Ironist most likely to claim the spots directly behind the leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lovers Leap Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Lovers Leap is allowed to dictate a measured gallop unchallenged and kicks clear entering the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Lovers Leap sets her own fractions from the front, the modest pace suits her stamina reserves over 7f, and she has the track position to repel late challengers on a flat course with limited room for wide closers to deliver.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Lovers Leap's lead is eroded in the final two furlongs and the horses tracking her have more in reserve.
scenarios.body: Dream Illusion and Ironist, sitting just off the pace throughout, time their challenge to overhaul the leader inside the final furlong; both have sound recent form at this trip on similar going and are ideally placed tactically.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sufficiently in the middle of the race to string out the field and leave a clear late lane.
scenarios.body: Izzy Fast or Angels' Share, racing from off the pace, finds clear daylight on the outside in the final furlong as the prominent horses tie up; Izzy Fast's course form and recent Goodwood win on similar ground make her the most credible of this group.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Prominent Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If Allegrino or Galileo Charm successfully works their way forward early despite natural crowding and secures a prominent berth.
scenarios.body: Both are mapped to midfield against their natural inclination, meaning this scenario requires them to race outside their mapped role; William Buick's positional savvy on Allegrino gives this the slim chance it warrants, but the style mismatch materially reduces the likelihood.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether any of Allegrino, Galileo Charm, or Fantasy Obsessor attempts to push forward early and pressures Lovers Leap's lead — if the early fractions quicken it transforms this from a controlled solo lead into a muddling pace that could open the race up for closers.

Izzy Fast steps up from 6f to 7f for the first time over an extended absence of 41 days — if she handles the trip she is the hold-up horse with the most live form, but the distance question is real and worth monitoring in running.

Lovers Leap has a STYLE_FIT flag and has not run for 46 days; if she is not fully wound up after the break her ability to control the tempo from the front could be compromised, which is the single biggest threat to the dominant scenario.

Angels' Share has been beaten eight, nine and eight lengths in her last three starts on good turf; Cieren Fallon is a significant jockey booking but her recent turf form on this surface must be noted as a clear concern before taking her at face value.

races.name: Infobond Nursery

runners_data.name: Dubai Charm
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for Richard Hughes with Billy Loughnane up — finished 2nd on Good ground recently, showing solid form at 6f, but drops to 5f here and will need a strong pace to close into; not ideally suited to the expected slow-burn tempo.
runners_data.comment: Dubai Charm is yet to win but her form has softened across her last three starts — 2nd, 3rd, then unplaced last time. She owns form at today's trip and on this ground plus a strong speed figure, though the yard is out of form of late.

runners_data.name: Fly Test
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up runner who has run three times on Good going without winning, flagged as a horse who fades in the finish — Michael Bell yard in decent nick at 2/24 over 14 days but the tendency to weaken late is a concern on an uncontested pace.
runners_data.comment: Fly Test is yet to win but the form is trending the right way — an unplaced effort and an 8th preceded a promising 2nd last time. A rapid 13-day turnaround and proven form over today's trip and ground add to the case, though the speed figure is modest.

runners_data.name: Holi Scarlett
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner, most recent run a 5f win on Good, handlers will be delighted with conditions; William Buick's presence adds significant competence in front, and at OR 64 she may be the form anchor in this field despite a slight STYLE_FIT flag.
runners_data.comment: Holi Scarlett claimed a race last time out, capping an upward run from 7th through 6th and 3rd. She returns quickly, just 6 days later, with today's trip and ground covered, and the improving profile marks her a serious threat despite the yard's recent cold spell.

runners_data.name: Or Another
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type in the hands of Sam James who has run twice on Good and posted a pair of placed efforts — visor-wearing, returned after 42 days, but pushed into midfield by race shape rather than natural inclination; back-to-back placed runs on this surface keep him interesting.
runners_data.comment: Or Another is yet to win in this spell — a 4th followed by a 3rd before that. He does have today's trip and ground covered, but a 42-day absence and a modest speed figure leave him hard to fancy at these lowly figures.

runners_data.name: Sable Island
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and has shown ability to place at 6f Firm and 5f Standard-to-Slow, but only one comparable Good-ground run in three recent starts; Mason Paetel's 5lb claim could help offset weight, though as a true hold-up type displaced to midfield, the tactical picture is not in its favour.
runners_data.comment: Sable Island followed two solid thirds with a below-par 7th last time, yet she rates clear of this field on our figures — suggesting more to come. Today's trip is covered, and though a recent dip and 26-day gap are noted, she remains the one to beat.

runners_data.name: My Maria
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with only two starts — 3rd on Soft, 4th on Good, both at 5f — Kieran Shoemark for Archie Watson is a strong booking; style unknown which is a risk, but the Watson yard has a 2/32 strike rate and this runner could surprise with unexposed ability.
runners_data.comment: My Maria's last two starts brought a 3rd and a 4th, showing fair, consistent form, and she has run at today's trip before. A 32-day gap and a modest speed figure are the things holding her back from a stronger claim.

runners_data.name: Cydney Sweenie
runners_data.note: Three runs showing a best of 3rd, genuinely a hold-up horse by profile but mapped to midfield through force of numbers — the trainer's 14-day record of 0/6 is a concern, and a 43-day absence adds uncertainty; likely to be outpaced from a poor tactical position.
runners_data.comment: Cydney Sweenie's form has gone the wrong way, an encouraging 4th and 3rd undone by an 8th last time out, and she rates bottom of this field on our figures. She does have experience at today's trip, but a 43-day absence and a modest speed figure leave little in her favour.

runners_data.name: Miss U Gino
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse who fades in the finish and has recorded two 10th-place efforts on Good ground over recent weeks — the OR 57 is the lowest in the race and the form string of 500 reflects poor recent runs; as a redistibuted hold-up type who struggles to finish off, this is a tough ask.
runners_data.comment: Miss U Gino has managed only a 5th and two unplaced efforts in her last three starts, though she arrives with proven course, distance and going form. A 12-day turnaround keeps her fresh, but the modest finishes make her hard to trust for more than a minor role.

races.paceDynamic: Holi Scarlett is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with William Buick in the saddle, will stride forward on Good To Firm ground over 5f at Yarmouth — a track that rewards prominent positioning. With no genuine rival to press her early, she is likely to dictate a controlled, sustainable pace rather than a lung-busting gallop, which historically benefits the leader or those tracking close to her. Or Another, Sable Island, Cydney Sweenie and Miss U Gino are all natural hold-up horses who have been redistributed to midfield on the map because the field is too hold-up heavy to place them all at the rear — in reality they are unlikely to secure an advantageous forward berth, leaving the true closing run harder to execute from 5f. This race shape strongly favours horses who can race prominently or those riding close enough to Holi Scarlett to benefit from a compressed, uncontested pace — hold-up types relying on a late surge face a structural disadvantage against an unhurried front-runner on a flat, sharp 5f track.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Holi Scarlett Leads Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Holi Scarlett is allowed to stride forward uncontested and control the tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: She sets a measured, comfortable gallop and Buick delivers her perfectly balanced into the final furlong, grinding out a win on her own terms; her recent win at 5f Good suggests the trip and going are in her favour.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse close to the pace tracks Holi Scarlett into the straight and outkicks her in the final 100 yards.
scenarios.body: Holi Scarlett sets the race up at a comfortable tempo and a prominent type conserves energy behind her before pulling away late; on a flat 5f track where a modest pace leaves sprint capacity in reserve, tracking is the next-best tactical position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Get Home
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace somehow quickens unexpectedly, stringing the field out and leaving genuine energy in the legs of the hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-expected tempo from an early jostle drains the leaders in the closing stages, allowing a horse with a sharp turn of foot to mow them down; given that most closers here are redistributed from the rear and unlikely to be in ideal position, this scenario is structurally compromised.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Late
scenarios.trigger: If Holi Scarlett sets too strong a pace and stops in the final furlong, gifting it to a fresher rival.
scenarios.body: She goes off too hard relative to her fitness level after a 6-day turnaround and fades inside the final furlong; a horse tracking just off her and still travelling could scoop the prize, though the relaxed pace expected from a lone front-runner makes this the least likely shape.

watchPoints.text: Holi Scarlett's early positioning is critical — if anything causes her to miss the break or get shuffled back, the entire race shape changes and hold-up horses gain a meaningful upgrade.

Or Another returns after 42 days and wears a visor — watch for early market moves suggesting the K R Burke team have targeted this race with a fresh horse, as his form figures on Good ground are decent.

My Maria is lightly raced and largely unexposed — Kieran Shoemark and Archie Watson together on an unknown quantity at 5f Good can produce unexpected performances; watch how she jumps and where she settles.

Fly Test's tendency to fade in the finish is flagged, but Cieren Fallon may attempt to use her naturally further forward than her H-style rating suggests — if she presses Holi Scarlett into a faster pace it changes the dynamics materially.

The Good To Firm going (confirmed in the going report despite the input labelling it Good) plays to a fast-ground type — check for any drying that accelerates the ground further before the race, which could stretch the advantage of an established front-runner.

races.name: ATI Tank Hire Memorial Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Raneem
runners_data.note: Roger Varian filly with a debut win over 7f on Good ground, stepping up to a mile on similar fast conditions — the trip extension looks well within range, she wears a hood (h), and 24 days fresh suits Varian's pattern; sits naturally in a prominent role and is ideally placed to chase a non-pressured leader.

runners_data.name: Starlight Lass
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden have her back quickly at 12 days, and her form reads a win at 8f on Good followed by a second at 7f on Soft — the mile trip and Good to Firm ground are squarely in her comfort zone; confirmed front-runner who sets the tempo here, but rated at a STYLE_FIT of 0.90 suggesting she may not always command the lead comfortably when challenged.

runners_data.name: Dream Vega
runners_data.note: Ed Walker filly whose two runs at 7f on Good produced a second and a fourth — she has competing ability but has not yet won; naturally a prominent-racing type, she is pushed back on the pace map because Starlight Lass and Raneem fill those slots, meaning she will need to do more work than ideal from a position that does not suit her race-riding pattern.

runners_data.name: Sakura Impact
runners_data.note: Debut runner for a trainer with minimal recent strike rate (0 from 1 in 14 days), carrying no going data, no form string, and no distance history — styled as a midfield type by default, shown at the rear only because the field is light on true hold-up horses; entirely unexposed and must be treated with maximum uncertainty.

races.paceDynamic: Starlight Lass is the confirmed front-runner and, with only four runners and no genuine challenger for the lead, she should settle into a comfortable, uncontested gallop from the outset on Good to Firm ground at Yarmouth over a flat mile. Raneem will track closely in a prominent role, while Dream Vega — a natural prominent type redistributed to midfield on the pace map because there is insufficient room at the front for all pace-committed horses — is unlikely to secure her preferred position and will find herself racing further back than ideal. The field holds more prominent/front-running types than can simultaneously hold those positions, with Starlight Lass and Raneem most likely to actually secure the favoured early slots, leaving Dream Vega squeezed back. This controlled, even tempo over a flat mile on quick ground sets up perfectly for a horse that can sit close to the pace and produce a sustained finishing effort — the prominent-to-front profile benefits most, as there is no pressure to force an early pace and no late rush from genuine hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Starlight Lass Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Starlight Lass dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and Raneem tracks smoothly throughout.
scenarios.body: Starlight Lass sets a sustainable clip on Good to Firm ground and, without pressure, finds enough in the tank to repel challenges in the final two furlongs; Raneem, travelling prominently throughout, is best placed to mount the only credible challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Raneem Sweeps Past Late
scenarios.trigger: If Raneem times her challenge perfectly and Starlight Lass ties up marginally after setting a stronger-than-expected pace.
scenarios.body: Raneem's one career run produced a win at 7f on Good ground and she steps up in trip here with form that suggests she can finish strongly; if Starlight Lass misjudges pace and flattens out, Raneem's sustained gallop carries her clear.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Dream Vega Finds Gap Late
scenarios.trigger: If Dream Vega recovers her natural prominent position from an awkward early situation and the pace is genuinely strong enough to set up a finisher.
scenarios.body: Dream Vega is a natural prominent racer whose two runs at 7f on Good suggest she can compete at this level, but she is displaced on the pace map and would need things to go wrong ahead of her; her STYLE_FIT tag tempers confidence that she can reproduce her best from a rearward berth.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Sakura Impact Upsets
scenarios.trigger: If Sakura Impact's unknown profile conceals a powerful late run and the pace dries up the leaders on fast ground.
scenarios.body: Sakura Impact is a complete unknown — lightly raced, no going data, mapped to hold-up only by redistribution, and trained by a yard with minimal recent form — meaning any success would depend entirely on unexposed ability producing a surprise; the absence of any historical evidence makes this the least reliable scenario.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Dream Vega's jockey Kieran Shoemark attempts to push forward from the gate to reclaim a prominent position — if she does, she could crowd Raneem and unsettle the early order entirely.

Sakura Impact's complete absence of form data is a genuine wildcard on quick going; Harry Burns (3lb claimer) riding a debutante in a small field on fast ground could produce an unpredictable early position.
Starlight Lass is back in just 12 days — monitor her pre-race condition in the paddock, as a horse asked to front-run on Good to Firm ground on a quick turnaround could weaken if not fully wound up.

Raneem's headgear (hood) is worth noting as it was worn on her winning debut — confirming it is fitted again here suggests the team expects it to replicate that focused, prominent-tracking performance.

With only four runners on a flat mile at Yarmouth, the pace is likely to be moderate rather than searching — this strongly rewards horses travelling close to Starlight Lass rather than those waiting off the pace.

races.name: Great Yarmouth Racecourse Maiden Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Ancestor
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced William Haggas-trained three-year-old with a single run showing a fourth over 10f on Good — style unknown so could race anywhere in the field, but Haggas in strong current form (13/49 over 14 days) and Cieren Fallon in the plate add significant class and tactical flexibility to this runner.

runners_data.name: Kokbastau
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's two-year-old returns after a lengthy 292-day absence following a sixth on Soft over 8f — the step up in trip to 1m2f and the switch to faster ground are unknowns, and the significant layoff makes fitness the primary concern for this natural hold-up type.

runners_data.name: Traveling Man
runners_data.note: Placed twice over 10f including on Good ground, this genuine hold-up horse for Charlie Fellowes has the most transferable form in the field for this trip and going combination; Daniel Muscutt rides and the 19-day turnaround is straightforward, though the trainer's 1/25 recent strike rate tempers enthusiasm slightly.

runners_data.name: Waterford Castle
runners_data.note: George Boughey's consistent placegetter has five runs of solid placed form, most recently second over 12f on Good — a natural come-from-behind operator that the pace map has pushed into midfield due to the volume of hold-up horses, so its chance is contingent on a late-run shape that may not fully materialise.

runners_data.name: Hollywell Stream
runners_data.note: Jane Chapple-Hyam's filly showed a second over 10f on Good and is a confirmed hold-up type that has been displaced into midfield on the map — William Buick is an obvious upgrade in the saddle, and her placed form on similar going is genuine, but she races slightly out of her natural role in this configuration.

runners_data.name: Seacole
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's lightly-raced three-year-old was placed second over 10f on Good at the only start — headgear (h) noted, style unconfirmed, and with a high OR of 120 this is a notable runner; Beckett's powerful operation (8/58 in 14 days) and Hector Crouch provide strong support for what is essentially a horse with everything still to prove.

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front-runner in a six-runner field, this 1m2f maiden on Good to Firm ground at Yarmouth is set to be run at a measured, even tempo until the pace quickens in the home straight. Ancestor and Seacole are both unraced or lightly-raced unknowns whose style profiles are unconfirmed, meaning nobody is nailed on to stride forward and dictate, while Kokbastau, Traveling Man, Waterford Castle, and Hollywell Stream all carry hold-up or prominent tendencies that push them towards the rear end of the field. The field actually contains more hold-up types than the pace map can accommodate at the rear — Waterford Castle and Hollywell Stream are genuine come-from-behind horses displaced into midfield on the map, though in practice they are likely to be hunting the back of the field alongside Kokbastau and Traveling Man. The tactical verdict is clear: with no horse likely to stride clear early and set a genuine tempo, this race shape strongly favours horses who can travel smoothly in mid-to-rear positions, produce a sustained finish on fast ground, and whose class and jockey quality give them the ability to pounce when the sprint for home develops — a profile that benefits genuine quality closers and those with proven form on similar Good to Firm going.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sprint Finish From Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If no horse establishes a lead and the field bunches into a steadily-run race that becomes a dash home from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: With the tempo compressed and every runner converging late, the horse with the highest cruising speed and best finishing kick on fast ground wins — class becomes the decisive factor over positional tactics.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely slow and the field strings out only in the final furlong, rewarding the deepest closer.
scenarios.body: Traveling Man and Kokbastau, comfortable at the rear, can produce sustained late momentum on Good to Firm ground if there is sufficient daylight; Traveling Man's placed form over 10 furlongs on Good going makes him a live candidate in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Lightly-Raced Type Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Ancestor or Seacole — both unknown quantities style-wise — elects to race prominently and sets a controlled, steady tempo that suits a front-running performance.
scenarios.body: A horse that travels in the first two at a moderate pace on fast ground and quickens two out can steal a healthy winning margin before the hold-up horses organise their challenge; Ancestor's trainer Haggas form (13/49 in 14 days) and a single run on Good ground offers some encouragement for this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Waterford Castle or Hollywell Stream overcomes their redistribution disadvantage and forces to the front or close to the pace earlier than expected.
scenarios.body: Both are true hold-up types racing out of their natural role, so this shape requires significant positional compromise and is therefore the least likely of the four; however, Waterford Castle's consistent placed record (three places from five runs) means a surprise front-end effort cannot be entirely dismissed.

watchPoints.text: Ancestor and Seacole — both carry OR=120 and are lightly raced with unconfirmed styles; whichever of these two travels most fluently in the sprint-finish scenario shapes the result, and their unknown tactical profiles make them the biggest wildcards in race-reading.

Traveling Man's hold-up style is well-suited to a slow-run race that develops into a late sprint, but Daniel Muscutt must find clear daylight in a field of six — any traffic trouble in the home straight could easily cost this horse a placing.

Kokbastau returns from 292 days off for Roger Varian — watch how freely it moves in the early stages; a stiff novice run after a long absence on faster ground than its debut could see it drop out quickly.

Hollywell Stream and Waterford Castle are both natural closers that will likely race towards the rear despite their midfield map placement — if the pace is genuinely slow, the gap between them and the leaders at the two-furlong pole may simply be too large to bridge.

Going is confirmed Good to Firm for this race despite the race card listing Good — all six runners carry OK going flags, but the faster surface will sharpen the sprint finish and may particularly suit horses who have shown their best form on quick ground like Traveling Man and Hollywell Stream.

races.name: Marine Lodge Handicap

runners_data.name: Prefer The Sister
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up filly in form — won and placed three times in her last four — with strong similar-going record (1W, 3P from 6 runs on good) and James Owen booking a claim rider; at 1d since last run the freshness flag must be noted, though her recent 1-mile form suggests the trip is no concern.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out just eight days ago and already proven over today's trip and going, this mare is our top-rated runner here, backed by a solid speed figure; a couple of flat efforts at the start of this spell are the only blemish.

runners_data.name: Regal Guest
runners_data.note: Modest recent form (best of 10th, 5th, 6th, 7th in last five) and 41 days off make this a difficult angle; no wins or places on similar going from four attempts, and the 3lb claim of Harry Burns is unlikely to offset the pattern of underperformance.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in his last five starts, this gelding boasts a strong speed figure and switches to first-time cheekpieces for a possible turnaround, having raced over today's trip and going before. A 41-day absence and a run of modest finishes remain the obvious worries.

runners_data.name: Charlatan
runners_data.note: David Simcock's six-year-old is the lone front-runner in the field and will get a soft lead by default; his similar-going record is thin (1 run, 0 wins) and he is tagged as racing slightly out of role, but controlling the pace on a flat straight mile with no rival to press him is a significant structural advantage.
runners_data.comment: Finished runner-up four starts back and fully at home over today's trip and going, this gelding has the form to play a role. Yet to score in his last five starts, though, and untried for 41 days, those gaps are the main reservations.

runners_data.name: Bizarre Law
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane rides a genuine hold-up horse whose natural instinct is to race from off the pace — pushed into a midfield map position because the field is loaded with closers; his one recent win came on soft (7f) and his best going figures are away from good, so the fast surface is a mild query even if the positional issue is managed.
runners_data.comment: A winner three starts back, this gelding has been unplaced last time and finds it harder to make the frame since, though he has raced over today's trip and going before and steps up in first-time cheekpieces. Recapturing that earlier level looks the key question.

runners_data.name: Heer's Sadie
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with the strongest similar-going record in the field (2W, 2P from 10 runs on good/good-to-firm) and a recent placed run; a true hold-up type whose natural closing style is compromised by the compressed midfield mapping — she is less effective when unable to produce a clean late run from the back.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in her last five starts, this mare did finish runner-up last time out, 28 days ago over today's trip and going. The earlier form in that sequence was modest, but the improved latest effort offers some encouragement.

runners_data.name: Rokuni
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with a deeply uninspiring recent form string (9th, 11th, 12th, 10th among last five) and no wins or places on similar going from nine attempts; the 3lb claim of Christian Howarth provides little assistance, and a tongue-tie tweak noted in headgear has not converted into results.
runners_data.comment: This gelding's form has crept forward across his last three efforts, finishing sixth only 12 days ago after a run of unplaced starts. First-time tongue-tie and visor add interest and he has raced over today's trip and going before, but he remains unproven against this company.

races.paceDynamic: Charlatan is the only confirmed front-runner in a six-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset on Good To Firm ground over Yarmouth's straight mile. Prefer The Sister sits at the rear as a genuine hold-up type, but the three redistributed hold-up horses — Bizarre Law, Heer's Sadie, and Rokuni — are all true closers who are unlikely to get their natural position and will crowd the midfield, creating a compressed shape behind the leader. The field holds more hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear, with Bizarre Law (recent winner, prominent headgear) and Heer's Sadie (best sim-going record) most likely to actually push forward and fill the midfield slots. A single uncontested front-runner on fast ground over a flat straight mile sets up a race that clearly favours a prominent or tracking profile, with Charlatan able to conserve energy and kick, while pure hold-up horses face a tighter closing window than they would prefer.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Charlatan Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Charlatan gets a clean break and dictates an honest but unhurried pace with no pressure from behind.
scenarios.body: Charlatan rolls along uncontested and arrives at the final two furlongs with a lead he can convert into a winning kick on this fast Yarmouth surface; his proximity to the pace throughout means he is never in trouble positionally.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closer Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely strong enough to set up a late run from one of the hold-up types finding clear air.
scenarios.body: A horse who gets a gap approaching the final furlong finishes with real purpose, but this requires a stronger-than-expected tempo given only one genuine front-runner; the redistribution of Bizarre Law or Heer's Sadie into midfield actually helps them mount a challenge rather than a pure hold-up run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Quickens Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is moderate enough that a midfield tracker picks a gap two furlongs out and outkicks the front-runner.
scenarios.body: Bizarre Law, with recent winning form and prominent headgear, or Heer's Sadie, who has strong similar-going figures, arrives on the heels of Charlatan and delivers a sharp turn of foot on the fast surface; the compressed midfield group makes this a crowded move and only a horse who finds clear daylight benefits.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Rank Outsider Upsets
scenarios.trigger: If Charlatan weakens sharply after a solo lead and the field closes en masse in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Regal Guest or Rokuni, both of whom have poor recent form figures, sneak into contention as the field compresses but their respective form strings and poor similar-going records make this a low-probability outcome.

watchPoints.text: Charlatan is uncontested up front — watch whether Daniel Muscutt uses that advantage to set a crawl that makes him very difficult to peg back in the straight on fast ground.

Bizarre Law and Heer's Sadie are true closers mapped into midfield — watch for crowding and interference two furlongs out as multiple hold-up types converge in a compressed group without room to make their move simultaneously.

Prefer The Sister ran just one day ago and is flagged for recency; watch her early in the race for any signs that the quick turnaround has blunted her sharpness, particularly given her hold-up style demands a late effort.

The going report confirms Good To Firm for this 4:15 race despite the card headline reading Good — fast ground over Yarmouth's flat straight mile will place a premium on clean positioning and penalise any horse caught wide or in traffic late.

Regal Guest returns after 41 days off with no similar-going form to speak of — watch to see if George Margarson's runner shows any early work in market moves, as the stable has a flat 0/11 record over the past 14 days.

races.name: Haven Handicap

runners_data.name: Zaraquelle
runners_data.note: 332 days off the track is a significant concern for a two-year-old stepping back in after nearly a year; Mason Paetel (5lb claimer) takes the ride for Ed Dunlop, and similar-going figures (4/9 runs, 0 wins, 1 place) do not inspire, though the visor worn previously is absent today suggesting connections may be simplifying the task.
runners_data.comment: Zaraquelle is yet to win, but her form is heading the right way — a 3rd last time followed a 5th, 7th and 8th earlier in this sequence. First-time tongue-tie adds interest, and she rates the clear form pick of this race on our figures.

runners_data.name: Divot
runners_data.note: William Knight's four-year-old arrives on a 25-day turnaround with a consistent placed record over 1m2f on Standard surfaces, and Cieren Fallon's booking is a notable positive; the jump to Good to Firm on turf from an all-weather base is the key unknown, though the horse's hold-up style gives it tactical flexibility if the pace plays out slowly.
runners_data.comment: Divot is yet to win, and the profile has faded lately — a 2nd and two 3rds earlier in this sequence gave way to a 5th and then a 7th last time. He does have today's trip and ground covered, but the recent dip is the obvious worry.

runners_data.name: Zafaan
runners_data.note: The only natural front-runner in the field, Charlie Clover's six-year-old won 12 days ago and has an excellent 2W5P record across eight similar-going starts; Billy Loughnane can dictate unopposed, but the STYLE_FIT tag (0.93) is a reminder that any pressure or positional disruption would reduce his effectiveness, and he carries a career-high weight burden here.
runners_data.comment: Zafaan landed a race last time, having also won earlier in this sequence either side of three 5ths, and a rapid 12-day turnaround points to a horse fit and firing. Today's trip and ground are both proven, with a strong speed figure adding to the threat.

runners_data.name: Spaceage Love Song
runners_data.note: Michael Bell's four-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse pushed into a midfield slot on the map because of field congestion at the rear — its actual racing style is late-running, and five consecutive all-weather starts on Standard surfaces make the turf switch on Good to Firm a live concern; Kieran Shoemark is an upside booking but 105 days off the track adds uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Spaceage Love Song landed a race in this sequence but has since found only middling form, including back-to-back 7ths, and a lengthy 105-day absence is the standout concern. A first-time visor and proven form at today's trip and on this ground offer some encouragement, though the long layoff is a real query.

runners_data.name: Sweetstevie
runners_data.note: Patrick Owens's four-year-old carries a ⚠ fade-in-finish flag, which is a material worry in a race likely to be run at a controlled tempo that compresses the finish; J F Egan rides and the horse does have a recent second on Soft ground (2/10f), but naturally a hold-up runner shifted into the midfield slot means it must overcome positional compromise as well as its own stamina frailties.
runners_data.comment: Sweetstevie is yet to win, with his last five starts reading 5th, 2nd, 9th and two unplaced efforts — a mixed picture at best. He does have today's trip and ground covered, and a first-time visor could help, but there's little here on our figures to inspire real confidence.

runners_data.name: Pure Theory
runners_data.note: Stephanie Cassidy's four-year-old has posted two consecutive zeros and ten placings from fifteen similar-going starts without a win, painting a picture of a horse that reaches the frame rather than wins it; Liam Wright (5lb claimer) takes the ride and, while the weight allowance is welcome, the true hold-up style relocated to midfield on the map leaves the horse facing a positional headwind on a track that suits prominent racers.
runners_data.comment: Pure Theory has been well below form of late — two unplaced efforts last twice out, a 9th before that, and a 6th, 4th and 5th further back still. First-time cheekpieces and a 60-day break offer a chance of improvement, and she rates above her official mark on our figures despite the recent dip.

runners_data.name: Sunset In Paris
runners_data.note: J R Jenkins's eight-year-old is the eldest in the field and returns on a 12-day turnaround after a string of poor finishes (9-9-4 recent); Jonny Peate partners and the horse's natural hold-up style, displaced to midfield by field density, means it must produce an uncharacteristic early move or rely on collapse in front — neither fits its profile on this course configuration.
runners_data.comment: Sunset In Paris is yet to win, and his last five starts read 5th, 4th, two 9ths and a 3rd — a mixed picture. He does have today's trip and ground covered, and first-time cheekpieces add a slight variable, but he rates bottom of this field on our figures.

races.paceDynamic: Zafaan is the sole confirmed front-runner in a seven-runner field and, with no natural pressers to challenge him, Billy Loughnane can dictate a measured, controlled tempo on Good to Firm ground over 1m2f at Yarmouth. The pace will be sustainable rather than searching, with Zafaan likely to bowl along two or three lengths clear through the early stages and dictate the fractions entirely on his own terms. Behind him, Divot, Zaraquelle, Spaceage Love Song, Sweetstevie, Pure Theory and Sunset In Paris are all genuine hold-up or midfield types who will be chasing Zafaan's back and relying on a meaningful late gallop to peg him back — and on a flat, relatively straight track with a controlled pace, that is not a generous setup for closers. This race shape strongly favours the prominent/front-running profile, and specifically a horse who can sit in the slipstream of Zafaan and produce a sustained run from two furlongs out; the field holds more hold-up types than the pace map can accommodate at the rear, and Spaceage Love Song, Sweetstevie, Pure Theory and Sunset In Paris — all true hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map — are unlikely to secure their natural wide, late position in a dawdle-and-sprint scenario.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Zafaan Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Zafaan bowls off in front at a steady clip and the hold-up pack fail to mount a sustained challenge on the flat Yarmouth straight.
scenarios.body: Zafaan sets his own fractions, never races faster than he needs to, and kicks again when challenged entering the final two furlongs; on Good to Firm ground his recent Goodwood win (OR=50, 2W5P in similar going) and front-running style make him the hardest to peg back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closest Chaser Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Divot or Zaraquelle track Zafaan closely throughout and outlast him in the final furlong with a sustained rather than sharp finish.
scenarios.body: A genuine hold-up horse who positions themselves just off Zafaan's shoulder will benefit most if the front-runner's stamina or weight burden (128lbs) begins to tell close home; Divot has placed at 1m2f on similar ground and Zaraquelle has top-of-handicap experience over staying trips.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses late and the redistributed true hold-up types find enough momentum to close down a tiring Zafaan from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: Spaceage Love Song or Sunset In Paris would need to thread through a compact pack while racing out of their natural position, reducing the likelihood materially given their STYLE_FIT discounts and modest similar-going records; Pure Theory's recent form string of 00 makes this further speculative.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic Shuffle, Surprise Winner
scenarios.trigger: If the field bunches tightly mid-race, creating traffic trouble that negates positional plans and leaves the result open.
scenarios.body: A messy race with seven hold-up types funnelling into the Yarmouth straight could produce an unexpected closer, but without a genuine pace injection this scenario is unlikely to materialise on a flat, fair track in a small field.

watchPoints.text: Watch Zafaan's early sections — if Billy Loughnane bowls off unchallenged and the split at the half-mile is uncommonly slow, the hold-up pack will be chasing shadows up the straight with no momentum to close.

Monitor Divot's ability to handle the turf and Good to Firm switch after five consecutive all-weather starts; if William Knight's runner travels comfortably in the first half-mile it becomes the most dangerous chaser to Zafaan.

Zaraquelle's 332-day absence (317 days for jockey Mason Paetel) is extreme — watch the parade ring for any signs of condition or freshness issues, as a two-year-old returning after nearly a year in a handicap is a high-risk proposition.

With four runners carrying REDISTRIBUTED flags, the bunch entering the straight could be compact and slow to unravel — watch for any traffic incident or crowding around the two-furlong pole that could affect the hold-up horses' late runs.

Spaceage Love Song's visor (hg:v) and Sweetstevie's visor are both headgear factors worth tracking — horses in headgear can race with more urgency early, which may inadvertently put Zafaan under slight pressure despite his lone front-runner status.
